contract.note: Demonstrated real-world competence is a fair ordinary reading of effectiveness. Marcus specifies neither human-level generality nor replacement of language models; treating world-model learning as an alternative approach is reasonable.

evidence.note: The 2022 research reports physical robots learning locomotion, manipulation, and navigation directly from interaction, including learning from scratch. These demonstrations meet the contract's capability and training-input criteria.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's fair plain reading, DayDreamer supplies a pre-publication counterexample: a demonstrated learning approach acquiring useful physical-world capabilities through interaction without extensive personal-data collection. The evidence does not establish unrestricted intelligence, which the statement did not expressly require.
